SwiftBar - Powerful macOS menu bar customization tool.

summary.one_liner: SwiftBar is a macOS menu bar customization tool that runs user scripts and displays their output as menu bar items and dropdown menus.
summary.what_it_does: SwiftBar runs executable scripts from a chosen Plugin Folder and renders their stdout as menu bar titles and dropdown menu items. Output lines can carry parameters for color, SF Symbols, images, fonts, tooltips, badges, checkmarks, hotkeys, and actions such as opening URLs, running bash scripts, or refreshing a plugin. Refresh intervals come from the filename (for example date.1m.sh) or from cron-style metadata. It is compatible with BitBar/xbar plugins and supports Standard, Shortcuts, Ephemeral, and Streamable plugin types. It also offers a URL scheme for refreshing, enabling, and notifying, plus environment variables exposing macOS and SwiftBar info to plugins.
use_cases: show system status in the macOS menu bar
run a shell script on a schedule and display its output
customize menu bar items with icons, colors and badges
install ready-made BitBar/xbar menu bar plugins
trigger scripts or URLs from a menu bar dropdown
show temporary notifications via the menu bar
how_to_run: Or download the app from GitHub Releases
Or clone the repo, open SwiftBar/SwiftBar.xcodeproj in Xcode, and press play
Launch SwiftBar and set the Plugin Folder on first run
Save an executable script named like name.1m.sh into the Plugin Folder
notable: Plugins can be any executable script in any language
Streamable plugins that update the menu bar from a continuous output stream
URL scheme for refreshing, enabling, and notifying plugins
Hidden defaults settings for advanced behavior such as Plugin Developer Mode
caveats: Runs on macOS Monterey (12) and later
SF Symbols are always disabled on Catalina
Plugin positions reset if the plugin filename changes
keywords: show script output in menu bar
